subject.title: Embedded runner: freshly streamed thinking signatures intermittently invalid on replay (Anthropic); recovery wrapper never fires because error text is genericized

question: Should OpenClaw stop replaying completed-turn Anthropic Claude 4-family signed thinking blocks as the durable prevention path, or keep the current preserve-and-recover behavior until stronger provider-contract proof lands?
rationale: Current source deliberately preserves these blocks, while field reports and open PRs show that preserving them can still trigger replay-invalid failures; choosing the default affects provider compatibility, prompt-cache behavior, and message delivery.

options.title: Land scoped replay prevention
options.body: Review and land a focused prevention PR such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383 once compatibility proof is acceptable, so old completed-turn thinking no longer poisons replay.

options.title: Stay recovery-only for now
options.body: Keep the current preserve policy and rely on the merged strip-and-retry recovery path, accepting that users may still see a failed first replay before repair.

options.title: Split by model/provider contract
options.body: Require a narrower policy that preserves only models with proven stable replay contracts and drops/scopes others with explicit tests.

recommendation.title: Land scoped replay prevention
recommendation.body: Review and land a focused prevention PR such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383 once compatibility proof is acceptable, so old completed-turn thinking no longer poisons replay.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent integration history on the async recovery path makes this the best available routing candidate for the compatibility/default decision.
